rows.name: The tidal Rivers Bure, Ant and Thurne
rows.message: Tide locking, where high tides restrict normal drainage of the river out to sea, over the next two days may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible from 3pm to 6pm on Friday 16 October and again overnight from 3am to 6am on Saturday 17 October. We expect to see high water levels around Potter Heigham, Wroxham boat yards and Ferry Road in Horning. Levels can take several hours to peak. We are closely monitoring the situation . Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 10:00AM on Saturday 17 October or as the situation changes.

rows.name: North Sea coast at Bridlington
rows.message: There is no longer a threat of flooding, though standing water and debris may still remain. The previous tide of concern has now passed, the weather is more settled and no flooding is expected. We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary. Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.

rows.name: River Cole, Dorcan Brook and South Marston Brook
rows.message: There is no longer a threat of flooding. Further rainfall is forecast. We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary. Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.

rows.name: South Devon coast from Start Point to Dawlish Warren
rows.message: High tides, strong winds and large waves tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible from 2 hours either side of high tide on Friday morning Areas particularly at risk include Torbay, Teignmouth, Beesands, Torcross, Slapton and Dawlish. The high tide at Exmouth on Friday is at 04:05 GMT, times of high water will vary along the coast. Forecast total high tide level is 2.03mAOD, which is 0.81 metres above tide table level. Strong force 7 north easterly winds and offshore wave heights of over 2.5m are forecast over the high tide. Coastal conditions should ease for Friday evening's high tide. We are closely monitoring the situation . Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 12:00PM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

rows.name: South Devon coast at Beesands, Torcross, Slapton and Dawlish
rows.message: High tides, strong winds and large waves are expected to cause flooding tomorrow morning. Flooding is expected from 2 hours either side of high tide on Friday morning Areas particularly at risk include exposed coastal areas at Hallsands, Beesands, Torcross, Slapton, Blackpool Sands, Teignmouth Promenade and Dawlish. The high tide at Teignmouth on Friday is at 03:55 GMT, times of high water will vary along the coast. Forecast total high tide level is 2.11mAOD, which is 0.75 metres above tide table level. Strong force 7 north easterly winds and offshore wave heights of over 2.5m are forecast over the high tide. Coastal conditions should ease for Friday evening's high tide. We are closely monitoring the situation . Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 12:00PM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

rows.name: West coast of Dorset
rows.message: Strong winds and large waves tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible from 03:20am to 11:00am on 23/10/2026 Areas most at risk include Lyme Regis, Charmouth, Seatown, West Bay, Bothenhampton, Burton Freshwater, Burton Bradstock, Cogden Beach, Chesil Beach, West Fleet, East Fleet and particularly at Chiswell. Further flooding is possible at Chiswell throughout the morning due to Storm Austin bringing force 7 to 8 high winds and large waves. We are closely monitoring the situation . Exposed coastal areas may be hazardous due to strong winds and large waves. Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded. This message will be updated by 2:30PM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

rows.name: Christchurch Harbour
rows.message: High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible from 07:15am to 11:15am on 23/10/2026. Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near rivers or on the coast. Areas most at risk include Christchurch Harbour and tidal stretches of the Lower Stour and Avon. The detailed tidal forecast for those who use it is for a peak level at Christchurch of 1.25mAODN at 09:15 with NW force 6 winds. (mAODN is height above average sea level.) We are closely monitoring the situation . Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded. This message will be updated by 3:30PM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

rows.name: East coast of Dorset
rows.county: Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole, Dorset Council
rows.message: High tides tomorrow morning may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible from 03:20am to 7:20am on 23/10/2026. Areas most at risk include Castletown, and Preston Beach at Weymouth. Other areas at Swanage Bay, Studland Bay, Sandbanks, Poole Harbour, Bournemouth Beach, Hengistbury Head and Christchurch Harbour may also be affected. The detailed tidal forecast for those who use it is for a peak level at Weymouth of 1.56mAODN at 05:20 with southerly force 7 winds. (mAODN is height above average sea level.) We are closely monitoring the situation . Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded. This message will be updated by 3:30PM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

rows.name: River Stour and Smestow Brook in the Black Country and South Staffordshire
rows.message: Forecast high river levels overnight may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible from the early hours of Friday 23 October . Flooding may affect low lying land and roads around Halesowen, Stourbridge, Wombourne, Kingswinford and Kinver. We are closely monitoring the situation . Avoid low lying roads near rivers, which may be flooded. This message will be updated by 11:00AM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

rows.name: River Churnet and River Tean
rows.message: Forecast high river levels overnight may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible from the early hours of Friday 23 October . Flooding may affect low-lying land and roads adjacent to the River Churnet between Leek and Rocester and the River Tean between Adderley and Spath including Cecilly Brook at Cheadle.w lying land and roads near rivers. We are closely monitoring the situation . Avoid low lying roads near rivers, which may be flooded. This message will be updated by 11:00AM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

rows.name: Lower River Soar in Leicestershire
rows.message: Forecast rising river levels overnight may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible from the morning of Friday 23 October . Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near rivers. Areas most at risk are low-lying agricultural land and roads including Slash Lane at Sileby and the Mountsorrel to Sileby road. Rainfall is forecast this evening. River levels at Pillings Lock Gauge will begin rising from 21:00 on 22/10/26 therefore this pre emptive flood alert is being issued. We are closely monitoring the situation . Avoid using low lying footpaths and any bridges near local watercourses. This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.

rows.name: Ings Beck and Oakenshaw Beck
rows.river_or_sea: Ings Beck, Alverthorpe Beck, Balne Beck, Oakenshaw Beck
rows.message: Rising river levels overnight may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible from the early hours of Friday 23 October . Locations most affected will be Alverthorpe Beck, Balne Beck, Ings Beck and Oakenshaw Beck in Wakefield, low lying land and roads near rivers. Rain associated with Storm Austen overnight will see river levels rise from the early hours of Friday, peaking between 6:00AM and midday. Friday will be largely dry with levels falling through the day. Further rain is forecast on Saturday afternoon which may see levels rise again. We are closely monitoring the situation . Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Friday 23 October or as the situation changes.
